props.gloss_en: Rabban Gamliel: the evening Shema may be recited until dawn
the mishnah: Rabban Gamliel's sons came [late] from a wedding hall and asked him whether they might still recite the Shema
what they asked was: do the Rabbis dispute you, or do they agree with you and say 'until midnight' only as a fence?
the sons' question: do the Rabbis dispute you (and then the many prevail over the individual), or do they hold as you do and say 'until midnight' only to keep a person far from transgression?
[where] an individual [disputes] the many, the halakha follows the many
the Rabbis hold as I do: the evening Shema's obligation runs until dawn
and you [who have not yet recited, though it is past midnight] are obligated to recite
their 'until midnight' is said to keep a person far from transgression

objections.gloss_en: ועד השתא לא שמיע להו הא דרבן גמליאל?! -- had his own sons not heard, until now, that he permits the Shema after midnight? then they could not have been asking what the narrative seems to say they asked

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קאמרי ליה -- they were not asking his view; they asked whether the Rabbis dispute him (so the many prevail) or agree and fence, and he answered: they agree, you are obligated, and 'until midnight' is a fence (= p_hachi_kaamri)
